{"url": "https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=all%3AHow+do+risk-sensitive+model+predictive+control+architectures+adapt+internal+parameters+in+response+to+longitudinal+experience%3F&max_results=4", "scope": "paper abstracts; preprints, peer-review status not verified", "excerpt": "title: A Framework for Time-Consistent, Risk-Sensitive Model Predictive Control: Theory and Algorithms
id: http://arxiv.org/abs/1703.01029v2
published: 2017-03-03T04:11:16Z
summary: In this paper we present a framework for risk-sensitive model predictive control (MPC) of linear systems affected by stochastic multiplicative uncertainty. Our key innovation is to consider a time-consistent, dynamic risk evaluation of the cumulative cost as the objective function to be minimized. This framework is axiomatically justified in terms of time-consistency of risk assessments, is amenable to dynamic optimization, and is unifying in the sense that it captures a full range of risk preferences from risk-neutral (i.e., expectation) to worst case. Within this framework, we propose and analyze an online risk-sensitive MPC algorithm that is provably stabilizing. Furthermore, by exploiting the dual representation of time-consistent, dynamic risk measures, we cast the computation of the MPC control law as a convex optimization problem amenable to real-time implementation. Simulation results are presented and discussed.

title: Risk Sensitive Control of the Lifetime Ruin Problem
id: http://arxiv.org/abs/1503.05769v5
published: 2015-03-19T14:02:24Z
summary: We study a risk sensitive control version of the lifetime ruin probability problem. We consider a sequence of investments problems in Black-Scholes market that includes a risky asset and a riskless asset. We present a differential game that governs the limit behavior. We solve it explicitly and use it in order to find an asymptotically optimal policy.

{"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=cognitive+architecture+models+distinguishing+between+transient+behavioral+states+and+stable+preference+traits&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"Dynamic Digital Detachment and Work-Family Permeability: The Interactive Regulatory Path of Personality and Cognitive Load.\", \"abstract\": \"

Introduction

Mobile connectivity has worn the work-home boundary thin for employees born after 1995, prompting some to deliberately disconnect from work-related digital channels during nonwork time. Whether this digital detachment reliably narrows work-family permeability, and for whom, has been obscured by static cross-sectional designs that treat permeability as fixed rather than as a process unfolding across days.

Methods

Using a two-week experience-sampling study of 192 digitally native Chinese employees aged 22-29 (53.6% women), yielding 2304 day-level observations, we modeled the trajectory of permeability with multilevel growth and cross-lagged panel specifications.

Results

On days when employees disconnected more than their own average, permeability was lower both the same evening (within-person coefficient about -0.31) and one day later (about -0.24), and this association appeared to strengthen over the sampling period rather than fade overnight. The pattern was conditional on a second-order interaction between stable traits and fluctuating cognitive load: among conscientious workers the association held even on heavy days, whereas among neurotic workers it weakened to non-significance once load ran high.

Discussion

Because the data are observational and longitudinal rather than experimental, we frame these findings as associations rather than causal effects. They nonetheless recast boundary work as a daily, effortful, and conditionally successful act, extend conservation of resources theory and boundary theory into the digital domain, and caution against uniform after-hours disconnection mandates in favor of support weighted toward overloaded and emotionally reactive workers.\", \"doi\": \"10.2147/prbm.s632561\", \"pmid\": \"42781609\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13600267\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscr…
